governed_construct: A call that persists user-generated content (a file, blob, buffer, byte array or data URL) to a storage service: Firebase Storage calls (uploadBytes, uploadBytesResumable, uploadString from 'firebase/storage'; compat Reference.put/putString; firebase-admin Bucket.upload / File.save) or another storage backend's write call (AWS S3 PutObjectCommand / Upload, Supabase storage .upload, Cloudinary uploader.upload, Vercel Blob put, etc.).
interpretation: The rule requires that user-generated content be stored through Firebase Storage. Each storage-write call in the file is one instance; it conforms only if the callee is bound (via import resolution, following aliases, namespace imports and method receivers to their declaring module) to the Firebase Storage SDK ('firebase/storage', 'firebase/compat/storage' or 'firebase-admin/storage'). A write to any other storage service is a violation, even if Firebase Storage is also used in the same file (all-instances semantics). The name of the callee does not decide the verdict: a local function or class method called uploadBytes that actually writes to S3 is an S3 instance, and a firebase-admin bucket.upload() is a Firebase instance despite its generic name. Files with no storage writes (e.g. Firestore reads, Firebase Storage reads only) are NOT_APPLICABLE. Downloads/reads and URL retrieval are not governed instances.
